extracted.intended_audience: researchers (especially early-career), science communicators, and the general public seeking to understand peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and resources for explaining, teaching and advocating the role, value and practice of peer review to researchers, early-career scientists and the public. Includes surveys, guides, workshops and discussion of peer review's purposes and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review's fundamental function
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is fundamental to integration of new research findings. It allows other researchers to analyse findings and society at large to weigh up research claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use peer review to enable scrutiny and to help both the research community and the public assess research claims; emphasises the role of peer review in integrating new findings rather than as an absolute gatekeeper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing the value of peer review with the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Sharing the value of peer review with the public is a central part of our work in helping people make sense of science and evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications about peer review should be targeted at public understanding — explain what peer review does and does not do, so members of the public can better evaluate scientific claims. This is an explicit organisational priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training the next generation in peer review and public engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensuring the next generation of scientists are equipped with the confidence and training in public engagement and peer review is a vital part of our work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide workshops and training (e.g., VoYS programme, 'Standing up for Science', peer review workshops) aimed at early-career researchers to build skills in reviewing, communicating science and engaging with public audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, accessible explanatory guides to how peer review works
rubrics_metrics.description: I Don't Know What to Believe — this booklet explains how scientists present and judge research using the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce plain-language guides suitable for broad use (the page notes the guide is used in BBC editorial policy, civil service training and high school education and translated into multiple languages). Emphasise clarity, real-world examples and accessibility for non-specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring researcher attitudes to quality, trust and peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality, Trust and Peer Review — 10 years on from the influential 2009 Peer Review Survey we have partnered with Elsevier to find out how far we have come. 3000 researchers were surveyed to understand how researcher attitudes have changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use large-scale surveys and longitudinal studies to assess perceptions of peer review quality and trust over time; report findings to inform advocacy and policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognising and debating the limits and roles of peer review (e.g., fraud detection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Related: 'Should peer review detect fraud and misconduct? What does it do for science and what does the ...' (page raises this question about peer review's responsibilities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge and discuss the contested boundaries of peer review — what it should reasonably be expected to detect (methodological flaws, interpretation) versus what lies outside (deliberate fraud may not be caught). Encourage debate and clarification of peer review's remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical, peer-led guides for early-career reviewers ('nuts and bolts')
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review: the nuts and bolts — a guide to peer review written by early career researchers for early career researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide actionable, peer-authored guidance focused on how to perform reviews (practical steps, checklists, expectations) tailored to early-career reviewers; combine with workshops and mentoring.
